evals.prompt: Here's a screenshot of the stats panel design — build it to match, using our existing CSS variables.
evals.expected_output: Target decomposed into a region inventory before coding; mapped to existing tokens; captured and compared region-by-region; bounded iteration; verdict with per-region table.
expectations: A layout/spacing/typography/color inventory of the target is produced before implementation starts
Values map to existing CSS variables/tokens before any new raw values are introduced
Comparison is region-by-region with quantified deltas, and exact colors/fonts are checked via computed styles or DOM inspection, not screenshots alone
Ambiguities in the reference image are listed rather than silently invented
Final claim of match is backed by a capture of the final state

evals.prompt: I changed the glassmorphism styles — visually check nothing regressed on the main game screen at mobile width and in dark mode.
evals.expected_output: QA-only pass: no edits; captures at mobile width and dark scheme; rubric-based delta report.
expectations: No source files are modified in comparison mode
Both the mobile viewport and dark color scheme are actually captured, not assumed

evals.prompt: Does the death screen match the mock in designs/death-screen.png? Give me a fidelity verdict.
evals.expected_output: Verdict-first report (match/near-match/mismatch) with per-region table and screenshot evidence.
expectations: Each mismatching region carries target vs rendered values

evals.prompt: Make it pixel-perfect to this mock. (Session has no browser or screenshot tooling available.)
evals.expected_output: Adversarial: capability check fails; the skill states visual verification is impossible here, does static checks, and does not claim visual fidelity.
expectations: The response states that no render/capture capability exists instead of pretending
Any checks performed are labeled as static (CSS values, structure), explicitly not visual verification

evals.prompt: In this repo: the EventModal should look like the reference screenshot after my refactor — check it and fix any visual drift.
evals.expected_output: Repo-based implement-and-verify loop with bounded fix rounds and honest remaining-delta reporting.
expectations: Fixes proceed worst-region-first with re-capture after each round
Iteration stops by round 5 with remaining deltas reported as a table rather than polishing indefinitely
